manufacturer: Linear Technology (now part of Analog Devices)
datasheet_id_and_revision: LTC6409 data sheet, document code 6409fb, footer 'LT 0517 REV B'; revision history Rev A 12/10, Rev B 05/17; copyright Linear Technology Corporation 2010
citation_convention: pN = PDF page index N; printed page numbers equal the PDF index. Typical-performance graphs are cited by title and graph code (e.g. '6409 G18'). Types: TYP; MIN/MAX at 25 C; MIN/MAX (over temp) = row marked with the full-temperature bullet; CURVE = read from a plot (vector path sampled after gridline calibration, cross-checked on renders); DERIVED = computed here, not printed. Unless noted, EC conditions are TA = 25 C, V+ = 5 V, V- = 0 V, VCM = VOCM = VICM = 1.25 V, SHDN open.
device_class: fully differential amplifier (differential in / differential out, VOCM pin sets output common mode); considered only as an alternative architecture (balanced TIA or post-amplifier)
input_type: not stated. Input common-mode range includes ground and the input bias current is negative (current flows out of the inputs, Note 6 definition), but the input transistor type is not named.
compensation: internally compensated; 'stable in a differential gain of 1' (p1). p16: 'intentionally compensated in such a way that its GBW is significantly larger than its f-3dB' (non-single-pole open-loop roll-off). Feedback capacitors CF across each RF are recommended at low gains.

min_stable_gain.value: differential gain 1 V/V, i.e. RI = RF, feedback factor beta = RI/(RI + RF) = 1/2
min_stable_gain.conditions: p16: 'Since the LTC6409 is designed to be stable in a differential signal gain of 1 (where RI = RF or beta = 1/2), the maximum f-3dB is obtained ... in this gain setting'; p1: 'External Resistors Set Gain (Min 1V/V)'. Recommended RI = RF = 150 ohm with CF = 1.3 pF across each RF (p16, graph G15 table).
min_stable_gain.below_minimum: Operation with beta > 1/2 (noise gain < 2) is not discussed. CF guidance (p16): CF in parallel with RF 'implements a pole-zero pair ... adds positive phase to the feedback loop gain ... boosts the phase margin'; larger CF reduces peaking and bandwidth (AV = 5: CF = 0.8 pF gives maximum f-3dB, CF = 1.2 pF gives no overshoot). p17: keep stray capacitance at +IN and -IN to an absolute minimum, 'especially true when the feedback resistor network uses resistor values greater than 500 ohm in circuits with RI = RF'.

supply.dual_or_single: single supply specified (V- = 0 V); split supplies allowed (bypassing advice p17; exposed pad must then go to V-, not ground, p8)
supply.recommended: 5 V (EC table also gives 3 V values); range guaranteed by the PSRR test (Note 10)
supply.source: p2 Absolute Maximum Ratings, p3 EC table

gbw.conditions: RI = 25 ohm, RF = 10 kohm, f_TEST = 100 MHz (GBW = gain at f_TEST x f_TEST)

gbw.value: AV = 400: -3 dB at ~23 MHz; AV = 100: -3 dB at ~114 MHz
gbw.conditions: VS = 5 V, RLOAD = 400 ohm, RI = 25 ohm, CF = 0

phase_margin_or_crossover.value: not given (no open-loop phase or phase margin anywhere in the datasheet)
open-loop |A| reaches 0 dB at ~2.7 GHz; roll-off ~25 dB/decade from 0.2 to 1 GHz and ~40 dB/decade from 1 to 3 GHz
phase_margin_or_crossover.type: DERIVED from the AV = 400 curve of G15 (see open_loop_curve)

open_loop_curve.note: No open-loop gain or phase plot is published. The closed-loop curves for AV = 400 and AV = 100 in G15 ('Frequency Response vs Closed Loop Gain', p7; VS = 5 V, VOCM = VICM = 1.25 V, RLOAD = 400 ohm, RI = 25 ohm, RF = 10 kohm / 2.5 kohm, CF = 0) merge above ~200 MHz; where loop gain << 1 the AV = 400 curve approximates |A_OL| (DERIVED: within ~0.5 dB above 300 MHz; at 100-200 MHz it may read up to ~2 dB low).

derived_magnitude_points.note: datasheet p16: 'the gain at 100MHz is close to 40dB = 100V/V'
resonant dip; beyond ~4 GHz the curves show package/fixture structure

open_loop_curve.reading_uncertainty: +/-0.5 dB on the plotted curve; plus the approximation error above

spot.conditions: input noise current density, f = 1 MHz, not including RI/RF noise

curve_points.note: rising at the end of the plot

current_noise.curve_source: p6 G18 (right axis); CURVE +/-4 %; plotted plateau 8.4 vs 8.8 pA/rtHz in the table
current_noise.hf_behavior: flat ~8.4-8.8 pA/rtHz from ~1 MHz to ~700 MHz, then rising to ~12 pA/rtHz at 1 GHz (end of plot); 1/f corner ~3e4-6e4 Hz (DERIVED). Values: 1 MHz 8.4, 10 MHz 8.4, 100 MHz 8.4 pA/rtHz.
current_noise.how_measured_or_defined: per input (noise model p12 Fig. 4 has separate sources i_n+ and i_n- each flowing through its own RF; output term 2 (i_n RF)^2). Measurement method not described.

noise_model: p12 Fig. 4 / equation: e_no^2 = [e_ni (1 + RF/RI)]^2 + 2 (i_n RF)^2 + 2 (e_nRI RF/RI)^2 + 2 e_nRF^2 (differential output); p13 Fig. 6 adds source and termination resistors; NF = 10 log(1 + e_no^2 / e_no(RS)^2).

input_capacitance.definition_notes: Only differential-mode input capacitance is given; common-mode input capacitance is not specified. Input resistance 165 kohm common mode, 860 ohm differential mode (TYP).

input_bias_current.conditions: input offset current, VS = 3 V and 5 V

input_bias_current.value: Note 6: IB is the average of the currents flowing into the inputs, so negative = flowing out of the pins

input_offset_voltage.value: common-mode offset VOUTCM - VOCM: +/-1 typ, +/-5 max (3 V), +/-6 max (5 V) mV; drift 4 uV/C

cmrr_psrr.value: output CMRR (VOCM to differential) 80 / 55 (3 V), 85 / 60 (5 V)
curves G10 (CMRR, 0.1 % resistors) and G11 (PSRR) not digitised; by eye CMRR ~88 dB at 1-10 MHz falling to ~65 dB near 1 GHz, PSRR ~82 dB at 1 MHz falling to ~51 dB near 1 GHz
0.1 % resistors give about 54 dB worst-case common-mode rejection (feedback-factor mismatch)

output_swing_notes: p9: outputs swing 'from close-to-ground to 1V below V+'. Output common-mode (VOCM) range 0.5-1.5 V (3 V) and 0.5-3.5 V (5 V); VOCM self-bias 1.25 V typ (0.9-1.6 V) at 5 V, 0.85 V at 3 V. DERIVED: on 5 V, IL = 0, each output spans 0.06-4.0 V, so the differential swing is at most ~7.9 V p-p with VOCM near 2.03 V; with the default VOCM = 1.25 V the low rail limits each output to +/-1.19 V, i.e. ~4.8 V p-p differential.

packages.name: UDB, 10-lead plastic QFN 3 mm x 2 mm (LTC DWG 05-08-1848 Rev A; not a JEDEC outline)
packages.exposed_pad: yes, pin 11, 0.90 +/-0.10 x 0.25 +/-0.10 mm strip (bottom view detail A)
packages.ep_connection: connected to V-; tie the bottom pad to V-; with split supplies do NOT tie the pad to ground
packages.notes: TJMAX 150 C; marking LFPF; grades C (0 to 70 C), I (-40 to 85 C), H (-40 to 125 C)

packages_source: p2 Pin Configuration and Order Information, p8 Pin Functions, p22 Package Description
pinout_notes: 1 -OUT, 2 +IN, 3 SHDN, 4 V+, 5 VOCM, 6 -IN, 7 +OUT, 8 V-, 9 V+, 10 V-, 11 exposed pad (V-). SHDN: CMOS input with 150 kohm pull-up, floating or high = active, low = shutdown (~100 uA). VOCM: internal divider (block diagram 200 k to V+, 50 k to V-) gives the default; bypass with >= 0.01 uF.
tia_notes: No transimpedance example, capacitive-source example or photodiode application. Relevant statements: (1) minimum stable configuration beta = 1/2 (p16); (2) CF across RF adds phase margin (p16; values in G15 table); (3) keep stray capacitance at +IN and -IN to an absolute minimum, especially with RI = RF > 500 ohm (p17); (4) load capacitance must be decoupled with >= 10 ohm series resistance per output (p9, p17), G16 shows +6 to +14 dB peaking with 1-2 pF per output and no series resistor; (5) 'Time Domain Reflectometry' is listed as an application (p1).
application_guidance: Optimum distortion with 200 ohm to 1 kohm load at each output (p13); RF >= 150 ohm recommended at gain 1 (p12); lower resistor values lower noise but load the output; balanced output loads; 0.1 uF || 1000 pF bypass from each V+ to its nearest V- (and to ground with split supplies), extra bypass for loads < 200 ohm; VOCM bypass >= 0.01 uF (p17). Typical circuits: ADC driver RI = RF = 150 ohm, CF = 1.3 pF, 33.2 ohm + 39 pF output filter (p1, p18); I/Q demodulator level shift RI = 2 x 75 ohm, RF = 620 ohm, CF = 0.9 pF, gain 12.3 dB (p21); single-ended to differential with 50 MHz LPF, 3.3 V supply, RI = 150 ohm, RF = 474 ohm, CF = 0.8 pF (p21); no-overshoot RI = 50 ohm, RF = 250 ohm, CF = 1.2 pF (p24). Measured output noise / NF (p14 Fig. 7, frequency not stated): AV = 1 (150/150, 1.3 pF): 4.70 nV/rtHz, NF 14.41 dB with 1:4 transformer and 600 ohm termination; 5.88 nV/rtHz, NF 17.59 dB direct 50 ohm source; AV = 2 (100/200, 1 pF): 5.77 nV/rtHz, NF 10.43 dB (transformer); 9.76 nV/rtHz, NF 16.66 dB (direct); AV = 5: 100/500/0.4 pF with transformer 11.69 nV/rtHz, NF 8.81 dB; 50/250/0.8 pF direct 14.23 nV/rtHz, NF 13.56 dB. NF at 100 MHz 6.9 dB TYP (shunt-terminated to 50 ohm, RS = 50 ohm, RI = 25 ohm, RF = 10 kohm; p2).
abs_max_and_input_protection: Total supply 5.5 V; input current (+IN, -IN, VOCM, SHDN) +/-10 mA (Note 2): steering diodes to either supply, and +IN/-IN protected by back-to-back diodes (p9: two pairs of series diodes) - if the differential input exceeds 1.4 V limit the current to < 10 mA; output short-circuit duration indefinite (Note 3, heat sink may be needed); operating and specified -40 to 125 C; TJ 150 C; storage -65 to 150 C (p2, p4, p9).
other_notes: GBW (10 GHz at 100 MHz) is far above the gain-1 f-3dB (2 GHz) by design (p16).
VOCM self-bias is specified as 1.25 V at 5 V (0.85 V at 3 V), whereas the block-diagram divider (200 k / 50 k) would give 1.0 V (0.6 V); RINVOCM 40 kohm matches 200 k || 50 k. Not explained.
The GBW and NF test condition RF = 10 kohm with RI = 25 ohm (gain 400) is as printed.
Output balance -65 dB (single-ended input) / -70 dB (differential input) typ, -50 dB max; common-mode gain error +/-0.1 % typ.
